name: dissipation_reentry
headline: At 3 bp / 60 bp the implied-vol DIVERGENCE re-entry (VIX >= 30 and >= 25% below its 30-session max while RSI(2) < 20; 3x for 10 sessions with a 10% burst stop) fires 7 times in 1990-2012H1 -- 2 entries in 2000-02 (burst P&L -1.7%, fwd10 mean +0.62%, 50% negative) and 2 in 2007-09 (-0.4%, fwd10 -0.05%, 50% negative) against the pass-1 trap's 26/14 at 77-79% negative -- and lifts a flat-1x realised-vol gate (cash when RV21 > 15%) from dev_1990 Sharpe 0.389 to 0.447 (CAGR 7.86%, maxDD -12.4%, 3.9 changes/yr, 52% cash, plateau 79%), passing all seven gates; but the model survives the two bears through the vol-level gate's 94% cash share rather than through the re-entry, misses the 2009 recovery entirely (+0.5% vs SPY +67%), and cannot catch the 1998, 2002 or 2009 lows because VIX peaked on the low day in each.
biggest_weakness: The crash protection is a realised-vol LEVEL gate at 15% with a one-sided knife-edge: at rv_exit 0.17-0.20 the flat-1x default re-enters the 2000-02 bear in its quieter stretches and dev_1990 Sharpe collapses to 0.19-0.30 (G6 passes only because the other five parameters are flat). The inference note rules this ingredient out for the 2020 regime (RV21<15% gates earn ~0% in Mar/Apr-2020), and it costs every recovery (2009 +0.5%, up-capture 52%, avg leverage 0.50, CAGR below buy-and-hold). The lens mechanism itself is statistically thin -- seven bursts, four winners -- and is intrinsically dangerous in a crash where VIX makes higher highs on lower price lows for >30 sessions (Oct-2008..Mar-2009): at vix_fall 0.20 it fired four times for -69% compound; vix_fall >= 0.25 plus the stop make it non-ruinous in DEV, not safe by construction.
